summary: Kenichi Kuranishi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an associate professorship at Taisho University (attested 2013-2026) and served as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii (born 1954) is a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1973 to 1982 and held a post at Kokugakuin University from circa 1993 to 2020.

Kenji Kinugawa (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971-1980) and under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida (~1975-1985), later teaching Eric M. Greene.

Kenji Matsuo (born 1954) works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973-1986) and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.

Kenji Shimada (1917-2000) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1938 to 1941 and worked there as a researcher from circa 1954 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop, also studying at Leiden University (2015-2016). He held a fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe (born 1949) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1978) and studied under Jozef Deleu around 1979 to 1981.

Kenju Kasahara (1851-1883) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and under Friedrich Max Müller (1879-1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell (~1879-1882).

Kenjuro Yanagida (1893-1983) was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida (~1921-1924). He held an academic post at Hirosaki University from around 1949 to 1950.
Kenkai Naganuma (1883-1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held a post at Kurume University and served as professor emeritus at Kyushu University from around 1947 to 1980.

Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979) and held an appointment as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe, and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk (born 1951) is an Indologist and historian who earned an MA at UC Santa Barbara and a PhD at ANU. He held posts at Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen, among other institutions.

Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and Sinology. Educated at Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY Graduate Center, he also studied at Peking University and held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883-1937) was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara (~1908-1912) and taught at the Pacific School of Religion and UC Berkeley (~1921-1935).

Kenneth K. Inada (1923-2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983-1999) and served as chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Stanford, Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He held faculty posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University, and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

Kenneth R. Valpey (born 1950) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held an academic post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth de Burgh Codrington (1899-1986) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, and held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1931-1948) and the University of London (~1948-1966).

Kenryo Minowa (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000-2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (2025).
